content: Auxilin, also known as putative tyrosine-protein phosphatase auxilin, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the DNAJC6 gene. The DNAJC6 gene is part of the evolutionarily conserved DNAJ/HSP40 family of proteins. These proteins play a critical role in regulating molecular chaperone activity by stimulating ATPase activity. DNAJ proteins can contain up to three distinct domains: a conserved 70-amino acid J domain, typically located at the N-terminus; a glycine/phenylalanine (G/F)-rich region; and a cysteine-rich domain that includes four motifs resembling a zinc-finger domain, as described by Ohtsuka and Hata in 2000. The structure of auxilin includes a protein tyrosine phosphatase domain and a C2 domain, both located near the N-terminus of the polypeptide. Together, these domains form a superdomain, which is a tandem arrangement of two or more nominally unrelated domains that function as a single heritable unit. The phosphatase domain belongs to the auxilin subfamily of lipid phosphatases. However, it is predicted to be catalytically inactive.
